themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Crown Heights is experiencing a sudden surge in complaints about dangling street signs and damaged trees this week, with dangling street signs up 2,300% (6 complaints this week vs. 0.2 weekly average) and damaged trees up 700% (6 complaints this week vs. 0.8 weekly average), suggesting possible storm damage or deferred maintenance creating safety hazards.
evidence: Street Sign - Dangling complaints: 6 this week vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 13.28, +2,300%)
Damaged Tree complaints: 6 this week vs. 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 5.42, +700%)
Illegal Tree Damage complaints: 3 last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 6.35, +1,100%)
Both spikes emerged within the same 7-day window, suggesting a common trigger
reporting_angles: What triggered the spike in street sign and tree damage complaints—recent weather event, deferred maintenance, or construction?
Public safety risk assessment: are dangling signs and unstable trees creating hazards for pedestrians?

themes_detail.label: Noise Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints in Crown Heights spiked 390% this past week (49 complaints vs. 10.0 weekly average), a statistically significant spike (z-score: 13.58) that suggests a new or intensifying source of disruption affecting resident quality of life.
evidence: Noise - Street/Sidewalk complaints: 49 last week vs. 10.0 weekly average (z-score: 13.58, +390%)
This is the single highest z-score spike in the dataset, indicating extreme statistical rarity
Spike is isolated to one week, suggesting acute rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: What is causing the sudden noise surge—construction project, new venue, enforcement activity, or seasonal change?
Interview affected residents in the neighborhoods with highest complaint density to identify the source

themes_detail.label: Sanitation & Street Cleanliness Decline
themes_detail.summary: Over the past week, dirty condition complaints jumped 318% (79 complaints last week vs. 18.9 weekly average) while street sweeping complaints rose 700% (6 complaints last week vs. 0.8 weekly average), indicating either reduced street maintenance service or accumulation of debris from the recent infrastructure damage.
evidence: Dirty Condition complaints: 79 last week vs. 18.9 weekly average (z-score: 5.29, +318%)
Street Sweeping Complaint: 6 last week vs. 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 5.42, +700%)
Unsanitary Condition is the 5th highest complaint type overall (654 total, last 90 days), showing persistent baseline problem exacerbated by recent spike
Timing aligns with street infrastructure spikes, suggesting potential causal link
reporting_angles: Has Sanitation Department reduced street sweeping frequency or crew capacity in CD 308?
Are debris from damaged trees and street infrastructure cleanup causing accumulation of trash and disorder?

themes_detail.label: Broad Complaint Surge Two Weeks Ago
themes_detail.summary: Two weeks ago, Crown Heights experienced an unexplained 161% spike in general/miscellaneous 311 complaints (45 complaints vs. 17.2 weekly average, z-score: 9.16), which has not been explained by specific complaint categories and may indicate broader resident frustration or awareness campaign.
evidence: GENERAL complaints: 45 two weeks ago vs. 17.2 weekly average (z-score: 9.16, +161%)
This spike predates the this-week infrastructure and sanitation spikes, suggesting it may have been a harbinger
Spike is now subsiding, indicating it was acute rather than sustained
reporting_angles: What prompted residents to file broad complaints two weeks ago—social media campaign, community alert, or underlying frustration?

themes_detail.label: Persistent Heat/Water Infrastructure Gap
themes_detail.summary: Heat and hot water complaints dominate CD 308's 311 record (3,877 complaints over 90 days, nearly 2x any other category), with no recent spike indicating this is a chronic, unresolved infrastructure failure affecting thousands of households year-round.
evidence: Heat/Hot Water: 3,877 complaints over 90 days (~1,292 per month), far exceeding any other complaint type
Illegal Parking (2nd): 1,998 complaints; Noise Residential (3rd): 1,047 complaints—both less than half the heat complaints
No spike in recent weeks indicates this is chronic infrastructure problem, not acute emergency
Community Board has not flagged this in budget requests (no heat/water entries), suggesting possible normalization of the problem
reporting_angles: Why has Crown Heights accepted such a high baseline of heat/hot water failures—is this a specific cluster of buildings or district-wide?
Deep dive: profile 5-10 buildings with repeat complaints; identify ownership patterns and HPD enforcement history
